newsitem.title: USA: Gingrich wants more B-2 bombers next year.
newsitem.headline: Gingrich wants more B-2 bombers next year.

text.p: U.S. House of Representatives Speaker Newt Gingrich told President Bill Clinton on Monday he would support congressional approval next year for additional B-2 Stealth bombers, and urged the president to ask for even more.
Gingrich argued in a letter to Clinton that U.S. cruise missile strikes against Iraq two weeks ago showed a need for the radar-evading bombers. They are built by the Northrop Grumman Corp.

The speaker said the 44 cruise missiles used in that strike cost $70 million. Two B-2s could have dropped 32 precision-guided bombs more accurately for $6 million at current prices and $600,000 in the future when precision bombs will be cheaper, he said.
Gingrich did not say how many more of the radar-evading bombers should be approved next year. Supporters want 40 of them eventually, rather than the 20 now planned.

Congress approved a mandate in 1993 that no more than 20 be built for $44.4 billion, but repealed the mandate last year. The cost of 20 more has been estimated by supporters to be about $12 billion and by opponents to be more than $20 billion.

Defense Secretary William Perry has strongly opposed buying more B-2s in the past, saying the Air Force does not need them and cannot afford them. The Defense Department is conducting a new study to determine future bomber needs.
